To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the steady solutions for gravity and gravity-capillarity flows are stable; (2) the solutions for the trapped waves are stable; (3) the solutions for trapped gravity and gravity-capilarity waves have a similar stability behavior; (4) the solutions for gravity waves with a train of trapped waves are stable.

1) the stability of gravity critical flow steady solutions is investigated, and it is found that the steady solution is stable to infinitesimal disturbances; 2) the stability of critical flow gravity-capillary steady solutions is investigated.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability of gravity and gravity-capillarity critical flows over submerged obstructions in a channel.
the stability of steady gravity and gravity-capillar solutions of critical flow over submerged obstructions in a channel.
the stability and instability of critical flows over submerged disturbances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the steady gravity-capillary critical solution, with a single or a train of trapped waves is stable.
gravity-capillary flows are always stable, and gravity flows are stable in the absence of trapped waves.
the stability of critical flows in the presence of gravity and surface-tension forces is very robust.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the critical flow steady solution is stable and the trapped wave steady solution is unstable.
the stability of the steady critical flow solutions is confirmed.
the stability of critical flows and trapped waves in both the gravity and gravity-capillarity cases is confirmed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability of gravity-capillary solutions is not necessarily better than that of gravity solutions.
the stability of the steady solution is not a good predictor of stability of the corresponding time dependent solution.
gravity and gravity-capillarity effects can be important in understanding the stability of critical flow solutions.
